source: Invest Like the Best — Why the markets are pricing AI wrong: July 2026 AI/semis selloff, private inference cloud, old-GPU repricing, ~$700B Blackwell/Rubin credit gap
summary: Regulatory risk is the single biggest tail risk to AI — the industry has done a terrible job of PR and data center moratoria could spread
summary_extended: Baker argues that regulatory risk — specifically data center moratoria — is the single largest structural tail risk to the AI buildout, and that the industry has done a poor job of defending itself politically. He points to New York's data center moratorium as the first domino, warning that a false but spreading political narrative (data centers raise electricity prices, consume water, and displace jobs) could trigger similar bans in other states or municipalities. Baker contends the factual reality is the opposite — data centers lower local electricity prices, create well-paying blue-collar jobs, and have minimal environmental impact — but that this story is not being told effectively. He calls for a coordinated industry PAC running mass-market advertising (e.g., NFL and World Series slots) to counter the narrative before it metastasizes into broader legislative action that could materially slow or halt the AI infrastructure buildout.
detail: New York's data center moratorium is the first of potentially many. The political narrative (data centers raise electricity prices, use water, take jobs) is factually wrong but spreading. The industry needs a coordinated PR campaign (PAC running ads during NFL/World Series) explaining that data centers lower local electricity prices, create high-paying blue-collar jobs, and have no material water/environmental impact. The AI industry's failure to tell its story is a structural risk to the buildout.
